before.title: 5.7L Hemi Exhaust Manifold Bolt Breakage
before.description: The 5.7L Hemi in the RAM 1500 Classic breaks exhaust manifold bolts due to repeated heat cycling. The driver side (left) manifold is most commonly affected. Broken bolts cause an exhaust leak that sounds like a ticking noise on cold start and a persistent exhaust smell.
before.solution: Extract the broken bolts and install new Grade 10.9 or stainless steel bolts. If the bolt broke off flush, drilling and extracting is required. Replace the exhaust manifold gasket. Some owners upgrade to aftermarket headers to eliminate the issue permanently.
symptoms: Ticking noise on cold start that fades when warm
Exhaust smell in cabin
Ticking from driver side of engine
Reduced fuel economy
Failed emissions inspection
Louder exhaust note

communityRecommendations.content: Apply anti-seize to the new bolts — this prevents seizing and makes future removal possible without breaking

before.title: Exhaust Manifold Bolt Breakage (5.7L Hemi)
before.description: The 5.7L Hemi V8 in the 1500 Classic is prone to exhaust manifold bolt breakage, particularly on the rear bolts of the driver-side (left) manifold. The bolts are subjected to extreme heat cycling and eventually fatigue and snap. When bolts break, the manifold develops an exhaust leak that sounds like a ticking or tapping noise, especially on cold start. The noise typically diminishes as the engine warms and the manifold expands to temporarily seal the gap. This issue has affected Hemi engines across multiple generations.
before.solution: Replace broken exhaust manifold bolts with updated high-strength bolts from Stellantis. Extracting broken bolt studs often requires drilling and using an EZ-out or bolt extractor — apply penetrating oil (PB Blaster) generously before attempting removal. Some shops weld a nut onto the broken stud for easier extraction. Replace the exhaust manifold gaskets at the same time. Consider upgrading to ARP exhaust manifold studs for a permanent fix.
symptoms: Ticking or tapping noise from engine on cold start that fades when warm
Exhaust smell in cabin when stopped or at idle
Slight loss of power
Exhaust leak noise audible from driver side of engine
Check engine light with exhaust-related codes in severe cases

communityRecommendations.text: ARP exhaust manifold studs are the permanent fix — they are harder steel and use nuts instead of bolts, making future removal much easier. Budget $80 for the kit.

communityRecommendations.content: Dorman exhaust manifold — solves cracking issues on many models

before.title: 5.7L HEMI Exhaust Manifold Bolt Breakage
before.description: The exhaust manifold bolts on the 5.7L HEMI break due to thermal cycling, causing an exhaust leak with a ticking sound that is louder on cold starts and quiets as the engine warms up.
before.solution: Confirm the leak by listening for a cold-start tick at the cylinder head/manifold area, checking for black soot trails, and inspecting for missing or broken manifold bolts/studs; a smoke test can help pinpoint smaller leaks. The proper repair is to remove the manifold, extract any broken bolts from the cylinder head, check the manifold for warping, and replace the failed hardware with updated bolts/studs and new manifold gaskets; if the manifold is warped or cracked, replace it rather than reusing it. Many shops replace both side bolts on the affected bank as preventive maintenance because thermal cycling commonly causes repeat failures. Typical repair cost is about $400-$900 for one side if extraction is straightforward, but can exceed $1,200-$1,800 if multiple bolts are seized/broken or manifold replacement is required.
symptoms: Ticking noise on cold start
Exhaust smell
Ticking decreases when warm
Visible exhaust leak at manifold

before.title: MDS Lifter Failure and Hemi Tick (5.7L)
before.description: The 5.7L Hemi V8 uses Multi-Displacement System (MDS) hydraulic lifters to deactivate four cylinders during light-load cruising. The MDS lifters are known to fail, causing a persistent ticking noise (the infamous "Hemi tick") and misfires on the deactivated cylinders. When an MDS lifter collapses or sticks, it cannot properly deactivate and reactivate the valve, leading to a dead cylinder. In severe cases, a failed lifter can damage the camshaft lobe, requiring a complete top-end rebuild.
before.solution: Replace all 16 lifters (8 MDS and 8 standard) with either OEM or upgraded non-MDS lifters. Many owners delete the MDS system entirely using a non-MDS camshaft, standard lifters, and an MDS delete tuner/programmer — this eliminates the failure mode at the cost of 1-2 mpg. If the camshaft has been damaged, it must be replaced during the lifter job. This is a significant repair requiring intake manifold removal and valley pan access.
symptoms: Persistent ticking noise from engine that does not change with temperature
Misfire on one or more cylinders (P0300 series codes)
Check engine light
Rough idle
Loss of power under acceleration
Ticking intensifies during MDS cylinder deactivation mode

citations.title: HEMI Lifter Tick HEMI MDS Lifter Failure - Hot Shots Secret

communityRecommendations.text: If you are replacing lifters, do the MDS delete at the same time. A non-MDS cam, standard lifters, and a tuner costs about $500 more than OEM MDS lifters and permanently eliminates the problem.
